config.title: Implement NonEmptyArray type

intro.title: Implement NonEmptyArray type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom TypeScript type called NonEmptyArray, which ensures an array always has at least one element. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's generic type parameters and tuple syntax to create this constraint. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system, including generics and union types. By the end, you'll understand how to enforce array length safety at compile time, preventing common runtime errors.
intro.usecase: The NonEmptyArray type is essential when you need to guarantee at least one element exists, preventing runtime errors in data-driven UIs. In e-commerce dashboards, product recommendation lists must always display at least one item to avoid empty states. Form validation often requires at least one selected option in multi-select filters or tags. This type ensures type safety when rendering charts that need minimum data points or menus that must have at least one navigation item.

objectives: Construct a custom NonEmptyArray type using TypeScript's type system
Apply the NonEmptyArray type to enforce array length constraints in function parameters
Implement type guards to validate NonEmptyArray instances at runtime
Manipulate existing array types by extending them with non-empty constraints
Integrate the NonEmptyArray type with generic functions for type-safe operations
Configure type inference to work correctly with NonEmptyArray in various contexts
Initialize and populate NonEmptyArray instances with proper type safety

steps.title: Define the NonEmptyArray type using generics
steps.instruction: Define a generic type named NonEmptyArray that ensures arrays have at least one element.
steps.hint: Use the TypeScript syntax: type NonEmptyArray<T> = [T, ...T[]]; This creates a tuple with one required element followed by any number of optional elements.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: generic type for a pair
type Pair<T> = [T, T];
